But you said it was difficult, you didn't want to yield, and I said: "Hmm. Listen, please, see to it, still see to it that ..." And so on and so forth. "... that the commission be set up, to consider it in all fairness and to determine whether it is necessary to do so. And in case it is, we shall see what the arguments are. We mustn't ..." And so on. And then further on I said that we must not -- that the whole case should be examined, that the Serbs should not be divided into various kinds. And towards the bottom, I said: "Then we should see. If she really needs to leave, then an option should be found, that it should be a transfer from one post to another and to vacate one. But dismissing someone and creating chaos among the Serbian people, we mustn't do that. It's better to stick with the person and to correct the person, to demand things from him, then to carry out a pogrom." And then it says: "You notice that Alija kept all his investigators ..." And can we please turn to the next page in B/C/S: "... who investigated him and beat him up in prison. They still work with the Secretariat of the Interior, even on higher positions." And then you say: "Okay, I have fully understood you. But just to let you know, there's going to be this problem in Ilidza. There's the issue of the secretary of the local community, Vojkovici. There's also some problems in Krupac, et cetera, et cetera." And then I say: "And why in Vojkovici and Krupac? And then you say: "The same situation. The people will not hear of that secretary, they just won't, and there has been a competition and the election will follow, because they cannot even prove legally that the regulation is against the law. They simply don't want him." And then I say: "Well, that won't do. It mustn't be done that way. Believe me, Mr. Prstojevic, this is precisely what must not happen. They cannot prove that he did something wrong, but they still don't want him, they cannot not want him, they cannot not want him. This is a professional post. It is not a post to which someone has to be elected. You have to prevent that both in Krupac and then in the other place. It mustn't be done that way. That would actually mean enforcing pure political will against the legal regulations. That mustn't be done. That is what the Communists did in 1945. No errors, no mistakes, but they don't like him. Please prevent that." And so on and so forth. Do you remember this conversation we had and the squabbling over the phone? It was the 11th of February, before the war, was it not?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this. I listened to this intercept, and I recognised your voice and mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the first conversation we had, and soon there would be no conversations thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the transcript further down: "Believe me, as a democratic party, we must not allow this. And as for the political will and for somebody liking someone or not, well, I wouldn't be socialising with half the people I co-operate with. I would steer clear of them, just as I would with any smelly cheese. But I have to stick with them, because I don't have the right to introduce the element of like or dislike." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page? Or, rather, no, there's no need for that anymore. You've had a chance to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This intercept was used as proof of my intention to take control of the municipalities around Sarajevo, to seize power there, and this is part of our pre-trial brief. Mr. Prstojevic, in our language, could you make a distinction between "take" and "retake"? Would "take" not mean that you are taking something, whereas "retake," that you are taking it from someone else?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, clearly, that is the distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you recall, we were criticised by people of having taken power at the elections and that we had handed over some important positions to experts. I believe that the man you had in your municipality was not a member of the party either.

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. Not even Mr. Kovac, the chief of the police station, was a member of the party. The commander of the TO staff, Dragan Markovic, was not a member of the party, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the war, when we were still hoping that there would be no war, that a transformation would take part and that we would be given our republic, if at that point in time I say at our plenum sessions, Please take the power in your hands, am I referring to the fact that we should take charge of things or that we should take power from someone else?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite clear that what you mean is legal and legitimate taking of what belongs to us. Before the war, we didn't have a firm footing, because the administration that had been there from before was still in power, it had a firm grip. And to put it simply, we weren't used to exercising power, to being in power.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If the document has not been admitted, I'd like to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1219, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, it follows from this conversation that you weren't all that frightened of me. Do you know anyone else who was?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, this conversation ended with me sticking to my position and saying that we would adhere to the law in everything we do. So despite all the discussions we had, I stuck by my view. Second, I don't know of anyone who was frightened of you. Third, 1995, after the Dayton, Mr. Krajisnik's office was against me going to Tuzla when the president of the US was supposed to come there. Only two mayors went there, those of Banja Luka and Ilidza, and our metropolitan. And regardless of the view of the office, I went there. In that same year when State Secretary Warren Christopher came to Sarajevo, when the security of the Serbs was being viewed in light of the Dayton Accords, and the issue was discussed as to whether they could remain in federal Sarajevo, Krajisnik's office directly told me not to go to that meeting. The Banja Luka mayor obeyed that instruction; I didn't, just as the metropolitan didn't either. I didn't jostle for positions. I was forced to become the head of the Ilidza municipality. I led the party during the war on a voluntary basis. And after the war, I handed over the power over the municipality before the elections. My assessment was that this was in the interests of the people of -- whom I represent, and I would not have gone against my views or positions on any score had I not judged that this was in the interests of my people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this given a number? Can we have 65 ter 08715, please. 01875 is the 65 ter number. Page 46 in English and 40 in Serbian in e-court. I don't think that's the right number. It may be our mistake. It's a statement from 2003. 8175, it should be 8175. That's not the document. This could be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, you'll see the Serbian version -- or, actually, I don't know if there is one. There should be one, because it's page 40 in Serbian. It reads: "It can be seen from the telephone conversation that Mr. Karadzic asked that things be done the way he thought they should be done. However, I stuck by my position, which was that agreed at the inter-party discussions about the status of the secretary, and there was a certain legal form to it as well." Is this something that is consistent with the events, and is this something that you stated in 2003?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the part where it says: "See, practically, the transfer of power was carried out, and the last post was that of secretaries of local communes, so these were the least significant posts. Such a strong conversation between me and Karadzic is something that was due to the fact that we hadn't met before or shaken hands, and he wondered at the fact that somebody would refuse to automatically accept whatever the suggestion was made to him. And later on, he asked who was that Prstojevic, and what was his position. And as a person who was of some significance before, and where the issue of honouring the will of the people and the agreed procedure was at stake, I wanted the things to take that course without the interference of either me or President Karadzic ..." et cetera. Is this how it was?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Previously, I was a younger man, I lived in Sarajevo, and I was able to clearly explain all the various elements to that conversation, more than I am able to do so today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please put a pause.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this sufficient, to have this -- or should we have this page admitted only? I think we have enough in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this case, you probably want the page, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Tieger, so you want that page to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be preferable in this instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's fair enough. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 07177. We've had it before, 07177, page 71 and continued on 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From line 18, I will be reading in English, and it will be interpreted to you: [In English] "Q. Let me ask you first about both the power to appoint people and the power to terminate people. For appointment to positions in Sarajevo, did both Mr. Karadzic and Krajisnik have to give approval or one or the other or neither?" [Interpretation] Answer: [In English] "At this point, we should distinguish between various levels of authority, of government. Neither President Karadzic, nor President Krajisnik, interfered or got involved in the election of officials into the Municipal Board of the SDS or municipal assemblies." [Interpretation] Was this your answer, and do you stand by that answer today?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my answer, and that was true.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is what we have in the transcript sufficient or should we admit it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it his answer is continued on the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think we need at least the full answer, Your Honour, at a minimum, which, as the Court notes, continues on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, what you said, that Karadzic, Krajisnik, and I'll expand that to anyone on the top, had any of them interfered with the lower levels in the democratic election procedures of various representatives?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, Mr. President, it is absolutely correct that nobody interfered from among you in the prewar elections of the Municipal Board and various office-holders. There is one point which is unclear, which has to do with the Ilidza Municipal Board members. I set out from the railways company to take up the post of the economy secretary, and there were stories about efforts in favour of Bozo Antic becoming a secretary for the economy, and that's why I became a secretary for inspection. That was all, and there was nothing more than that. Now, at the level of town, since Mr. Krajisnik hails from Sarajevo -- I'm not really in a position to know this, but this was the middle level which was dealt with by other people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 08175, page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the convenience, shall we admit the two pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit D1221, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 08175, page 36. "SM" asks -- is this page 36 in e-court? From what I can see, 36 doesn't fit into the picture. There we have it at the bottom: [In English] "Was there anything specifically that you can recall that you were asked to do that you refused to do?" [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in English, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your answer, I will read it in English, because I am not sure where it is in the Serbian: [In English] "You see this case, and I think at the Assembly when I was talking, but that was the -- after this date. During the break, I kindly asked Mr. Karadzic to hear one question from me. He told me, in a very harsh way, 'It's enough to spend a minute with everyone, that's killing me.' So I did not ask the question, and I wanted to ask -- that I wanted to ask him. And for a longer period of time, it was visible that there was a pretty big distance between two of us. I did not have clear access to Karadzic, so these contacts had to be done by other people." Is this correct, and did you state this in 2003?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, and this is what I stated. But let me add something. It was only in 2009 that I got translations into the Serbian language from the interviews from 2003, 2005 and 2006, and then I had about 15 objections that were of crucial value, objections to interpretation or to what the investigator said from where I told one Jonathan Harris. I did not say that. Then there was a break, and then he continued after a pause and said, You said this and that. That was obviously malicious, but at the time I believed that investigators were interested in truth, rather than that they wanted to prove what was not truth. And I did not know how to oppose them sufficiently so as to request that people who were malicious should not take part in this, because I asked for Haris Silajdzic. There are errors here. This is correct, but in many other instances there are errors, and I have it here in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 27 in the English version and page 16 in the Serbian version, please, from the same document. I think it's 65 ter 07857, unless it's an error. I think it's the same document, but page 27. Page 27 in the English version and page 16 in the Serbian. I'm sorry, this is on the 27th of November, so we need 65 ter 07875. 07875, and we need page 27 in the English version and 16 in the Serbian one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: [In English] "Now, at the end of 1992, you were effectively promoted. You became a member of the Executive Board of the SDS, and you also mentioned yesterday that at one stage, you became a member of the Main Board. Was it your understanding that the manner in which you carried out your tasks in 1992 was approved by the leadership of the SDS?" [Interpretation] And here is your answer: "At the same session, at the same meeting that is called 'Jahorina ple num,' I do not remember really when that session happened. I was elected to the Executive Board and to the Main Board. That was not an easy procedure. Mr. Karadzic, in particular, was breaking, pulling the break for this appointment, he was pushing for another candidate. But Ilidza, as the municipality and its army, had a very strong authority among the people and among the members of the then Executive Board and Main Board. And some people worked with me in ZTP, and they knew me from the economy. And upon their constant insisting, I passed." [Interpretation] Is this what you said? Was it really like that, the way it happened?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was precisely that, what happened. And I got more votes than your candidate, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that we do not need to admit this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. If I could have a couple of bits of clarifying information. I saw this is from the 27th of November, and if I could have -- it would be helpful to know the -- if it's apparent to the accused, the starting point of the tape, that is, the time the tape began. It helps to identify among the several ones, if it's known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay, that can be done outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would really inform Mr. Tieger kindly, but I don't know. I just know that the page is 27. If it has been recorded in the transcript, we might move on to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last document for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have 65 ter 5356.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prstojevic, is it correct that the Main Board elects members of the Executive Board by secret ballot, and the Assembly elects the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the Assembly elects the Main Board. And believe it or not, I do not remember how the Main Board elected us at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the list. Is it the list of people who were elected as members of the Main Board on that day, including yourself, when you were elected in spite of the fact that I was backing up another candidate? Is this the composition of the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was this particular composition of the Main Board that was elected at the Jahorina plenum or perhaps later. I wouldn't know. But this is the one that I was a member of and worked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Instead of the "Main Board," it should be "Executive Board." Do you remember that many people participated in the election of these people?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct, the entire Main Board. I just don't know how they elected us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by what you said, that I tried on two occasions to recommend another member who was your opponent, a different candidate?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely stand by that, and that's truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did I have to sign this once the voting was completed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJELJKO PRSTOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly. Such were the rules, and you had to, because you had to honour and observe what the Main Board decided.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The English translation of 65 ter 30751, which we admitted as MFI D1212, has been up-loaded. So, as such, we will admit it fully. And I suppose Mr. Karadzic will spend about three hours more. How long do you expect for your re-examination, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At this point, I'd estimate approximately 45 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you have spent about six hours, a bit more than six hours. So if you could plan to conclude your cross-examination in two sessions on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to ask such questions that would elicit as many yes-or-no answers. If I manage to do that, then I could do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn for today, and we'll resume on Monday next week at 9.00. Thank you for your co-operation. Have a nice weekend, Mr. Prstojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of March, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.32 p.m.,
